clue.text: Stand with element calling for change of leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the opening letter of the word is swapped for another

blocks.note: sodium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A stand made of some chemical element that, someone insists, needs a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the head of SODIUM is replaced by P to give PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised platform on which a speaker or winner stands.

clue.text: Satirise standard figure British put down

indicators.note: putting something down means dropping it, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm
one's figure is one's body
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A satirist mocks the conventional British figure being humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure suggests a number or a public personage, but here it means the physical shape of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody is to imitate something mockingly, a form of satire; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Denied American will block odd views being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
blocking a path means standing inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A US official denies that an American would stop unusual opinions going out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight letters of odd views are rearranged and the A slots in after the first three to give DISAVOWED.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow is to deny responsibility for or knowledge of something, so disavowed matches denied.

clue.text: Greek character Manolis purchasing houses from the south

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer, which sits inside the run of letters
in a down entry, reading from the bottom means going backwards, upwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A Greek man called Manolis is buying property, starting in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Manolis looks like the Greek character of the definition, but the character is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is the twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Taking part of spymaster is Korean star

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A Korean spy chief is portrayed as a celebrity, as if starring in an espionage story.
explanation.walkthrough: Star suggests a celebrity, but here it is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped typographic symbol, which printers commonly call a star.

clue.text: Even son grasps minute details, regularly making nourishing spreads

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold within, so the following pieces sit inside the earlier one
regular intervals mean every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: square means level or even, as in all square
S is the abbreviation for son
M is the abbreviation for minute
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A fair-minded son pays close attention to detail, often laying out generous meals.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUARE plus S holds M and EAL, giving SQUARE MEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A square meal is a substantial, nourishing one, and a spread is an informal word for a big meal.

clue.text: Is no tea brewed here?

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a certain place has no tea-making at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a place where, playfully, tea is not brewed; the country name is jumbled from the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, a place a traveller might ask about as here, and the clue jokes about its drinking habits.

clue.text: Lay to rest artist dad disowned

indicators.note: to be disowned is to be cast out, so those letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: a painter is an artist
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An artist who was rejected by his father is finally buried.
explanation.walkthrough: PAINTER loses PA, leaving INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, which is what laying someone to rest means.

clue.text: State briefly hotel, like obelisk ultimately, will rise in desert

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped
ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept
in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the order is reversed

blocks.note: Iran is a nation state
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
à la means in the style of, or like
the final letter

explanation.surface: An instruction that a hotel, like an obelisk, will be built in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: IRAN cut to IRA, then H, ALA and K, all read upwards to give KALAHARI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is a large semi-arid sandy region of southern Africa, a desert.

clue.text: Stop bagging one's refuse

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a rest is a stop or pause
one is I, and one's read as one is gives I plus IS shortened to S

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop collecting one's rubbish in bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse looks like a noun meaning rubbish, but it is the verb. One's is read as I's, giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to refuse to comply or give way; both are verbs here.

clue.text: A lot must fancy revealing aggregate

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A large number of people must like something, judging by the overall figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum total is the whole amount when everything is added up, which is an aggregate.

clue.text: Teenager conceivably that's involved in film production

blocks.note: first meaning: someone still growing and maturing
second meaning: the chemical that brings out the image on photographic film

explanation.walkthrough: Film production suggests the movie business, but it is the darkroom process of turning exposed film into pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is still developing physically, and developer is the chemical solution used to process photographic film.

clue.text: Diminutive Dickens character having pasty appearance?

blocks.note: Herbert Pocket is Pip's friend in Great Expectations
size is a gluey paste used to coat paper or walls, so sized means coated in paste

explanation.surface: A small character from Dickens who looks pale and unhealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Pasty suggests a pale complexion, but here it means covered in paste, the glue called size.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pocket-sized is small enough to fit in a pocket, so it is tiny or diminutive.

clue.text: Bridge player Graham, say, not about to lead hearts

indicators.note: not here means without, so the next word's letters are taken away

blocks.note: Graham Norton is an Irish TV chat-show host
on means about, concerning
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A card player named Graham declines to open with a heart in a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: NORTON loses ON, and the NORT left leads H.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, and North is one of the seats.

clue.text: RAF officer owned car, MG Mini Convertible, I struck

indicators.note: struck off means removed, so that letter is crossed out
something convertible can be changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An air force officer owned a car, then an open-top Mini, and someone hit it.
explanation.walkthrough: One I is removed from the fourteen letters before they are rearranged. Convertible looks like a type of car; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wing commander is a rank in the Royal Air Force, above squadron leader.

clue.text: Oddball strides around in squalor

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric and out of order, so the letters are jumbled
around means surrounding, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric person walks about in filthy surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddball looks like a person doing the striding, but it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtiness is the state of being dirty, and squalor is filth and wretched uncleanliness.

clue.text: Enthralled sailors extremely excited to circle globe

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept
circling something means surrounding it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: AB is able seaman, so ABS are sailors
the first and last letters
an orb is a globe or sphere

explanation.surface: Thrilled sailors are wildly eager to sail round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absorbed is to have one's attention wholly held, like being enthralled.

clue.text: Way doctor comforts sick daughter entering nearby house, reportedly

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one letter is placed within the following word
reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
beside means next to, nearby
a manor is a large country house

explanation.surface: A doctor reassures a patient whose ill daughter has moved into a house close by.
explanation.walkthrough: Sick looks like an adjective in the wordplay, but it is the noun the sick, patients, in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedside manner is the tactful, reassuring way a doctor deals with patients.

clue.text: Guts skinned pink fish aboard ship

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, so only the inner letters are kept
aboard means on board, so one piece is carried inside the other

blocks.note: the letters between the first and last
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A gutted and skinned pink fish is taken on board a ship, like a galley scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Insides is an informal word for the internal organs, and guts means the same.

clue.text: Emotions in a mess, time spent that's hurtful

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so that letter is taken out
a mess is disorder, so the letters are in a jumbled state

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone's emotions are in turmoil, and the time that's passed has been painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The T is removed from EMOTIONS before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means harmful or offensive, so something noisome is hurtful; it has nothing to do with noise.

clue.text: One old outfit of Fergie's?

blocks.note: first meaning: joined together as one
second meaning: the football club Sir Alex Ferguson managed

explanation.walkthrough: Outfit suggests clothing, perhaps of Fergie the Duchess of York, but it means a team: Sir Alex Ferguson, nicknamed Fergie, managed Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: United describes things joined into a single whole, and Manchester United is commonly called just United.

clue.text: Love having in retirement small round gemstones

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the order is turned around

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
S is the abbreviation for small
a lap is one round of a track

explanation.surface: A retired romantic owns some small round precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Small round looks like a description of the gems, but each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones, often cut into small rounded cabochons.

clue.text: Admit being inexperienced when caught out

indicators.note: out means removed or dismissed, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: callow means young and inexperienced
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A novice confesses to being inexperienced after being caught out in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught out looks like the cricket dismissal; caught gives C, which then goes out of CALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone in is to admit them, letting them enter; both verbs mean permit.

clue.text: Mistrust hint

blocks.note: first meaning: a feeling that someone is guilty or untrustworthy
second meaning: a slight trace, as in a touch of garlic

explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion means distrust of someone, and also a faint trace of something, as in a suspicion of a smile.

clue.text: Go off male at first, as 11 may do?

blocks.note: a bull is a male bovine
to go off is to fall asleep, to doze

explanation.surface: Someone nods off, with the man first, much as a property developer might.
explanation.walkthrough: At first places the male piece ahead of the sleep piece. The 11 is DEVELOPER, here in the building sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A property developer may flatten old buildings with machinery to clear a site, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Humble and virtuous person, follower of fashion

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
ST is saint, a virtuous person

explanation.surface: Describes a self-effacing, good person who happens to keep up with fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Follower of places the saint after the fashion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and humble both describe someone who does not boast about their abilities.

clue.text: Negative aspect of Denmark's top individual team

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across entry is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
own means individual, belonging to oneself
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A drawback of Denmark's best solo player in the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A downside is a disadvantage, the negative aspect of something.

clue.text: Let in Liberal Democrat moderate

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the last piece goes between the others

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
to ease is to moderate or lessen
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A moderate member of the Liberal Democrat party has been allowed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal Democrat reads as one party, but it splits into its two abbreviations around the middle piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Leased is the past tense of lease, meaning rented out, which is what let means for property.
